svg.title: How the November 2026 US remote-access chip rule decides whether a data center needs a licence, and its key dates
svg.text: Does this data center need a US licence?
The new remote-access test in section 744.24, simplified. Purple marks the answers that trigger a licence.

g.text: 1. Does it hold advanced US AI chips or servers?
Export classes 3A090 and 4A090, such as Nvidia H100 and H200 parts
No: this rule does not apply
2. Can it supply more than 12,000,000 aggregate TPP?
Counted across linked sites, digital links included. Roughly 750 H100s.
3. Is any of that compute for a company headquartered
in China, Macau or another D:5 country?
Directly, through a parent company, or via a middleman training models for one
No: no licence under this test
4. Is it used only for a commercial recommender?
Ranking products or content. Generating text, code or images does not count.
Yes: exempt, but must report to BIS
Licence required, reviewed case by case
Operators already serving such customers get 90 days from the effective date

svg.text: Separately: any advanced chip shipped to Brazil, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore or Thailand
now needs a licence too, unless the buyer is a US-headquartered company that files the new reports.
Source: BIS interim final rule RIN 0694-AK50, released 16 November 2026. Simplified; not legal advice.
